terms.meaning: the 3D graphics library the app uses to draw shapes in the browser
a 3D shape made of a shape outline (geometry) and a surface look (material)
the outline of a 3D shape, such as its corners and faces
the surface look of a shape, such as its colour and how shiny it is
a container that holds several shapes so they can be moved together
a compact way to store a 3D rotation

sections.name: File setup, SUBSTATION_SET
sections.title: File setup and default part set
sections.what: Loads the helper tools this file needs, then makes a fast lookup of the substation part types and a default grey-blue colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: a set makes checking whether a part is a substation part quick.
sections.watch_out: If the substation list changes, the lookup in this file changes with it.

sections.name: material
sections.title: Standard surface finish
sections.what: Creates a matte, slightly non-metal grey-blue surface finish for each part.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared look keeps generated parts consistent.
sections.watch_out: Each call makes a new surface object, so changing one part's finish does not change the others.

sections.name: mesh
sections.title: Shadow-ready shape wrapper
sections.what: Wraps a shape with the standard finish and turns on shadow casting and receiving.
sections.why: Likely reason: every generated part needs the same finish and shadow behaviour without repeating the setup.

sections.name: box
sections.title: Rectangular block
sections.what: Makes a rectangular block of the given width, height and depth.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocks are the most common shape, so a short helper keeps calls readable.
sections.watch_out: Zero or negative sizes are not rejected.

sections.name: cylinder
sections.title: Round tube or cone
sections.what: Makes a cylinder or cone with a given top and bottom radius and height, using 20 sides by default.
sections.why: Likely reason: many larger shapes in this file are built from cylinders.

sections.name: beamBetween
sections.title: Bar between two points
sections.what: Makes a thin straight bar that joins two 3D points, as a structural member would.
sections.why: Likely reason: structural members connect two points, so the helper takes points rather than sizes.
sections.watch_out: If the two points are the same, the bar has zero length and will look wrong or disappear.

sections.name: addFrame
sections.title: Braced rectangular frame
sections.what: Adds a rectangular frame with four posts, a top beam and two diagonal braces to a group, at a set depth.
sections.why: Likely reason: braces give the frame a stiff, drawn-steel look.
sections.watch_out: The frame is centred on zero, so the caller must move the group to place it.

sections.name: containment
sections.title: Domed round containment
sections.what: Builds a round containment building: a cylinder body with a dome on top.
sections.why: Likely reason: containment buildings are often drawn as a domed cylinder.
sections.watch_out: The radius uses the smaller of width and depth, so a non-round footprint still gets a round shape.

sections.name: coolingTower
sections.title: Cooling tower shape
sections.what: Builds a hyperbolic cooling tower by spinning a curved outline around a vertical axis, with a rim on top.
sections.why: Likely reason: the curved outline copies the shape of real cooling towers.
sections.watch_out: The outline uses only 18 steps up the height, so very tall towers may look faceted.

sections.name: turbineHall
sections.title: Turbine hall with ribs
sections.what: Builds a long box for a turbine hall, adds vertical ribs along its length, and a rail near the top.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The ribs and rail look like structural detail added to a box.
sections.watch_out: Rib spacing is at least 3 units, so short halls get few ribs.

summary: Builds the 3D shapes (boxes, cylinders, beams, towers, frames and many industrial parts) that the app draws for each project component, and sets their default look and shadow behaviour.
purpose: Turns a component's kind and size into a 3D model that the viewer can show. Lines 1 to 120 were supplied for this review. The rest of the file was not, so its sections are not described here.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The file keeps shape-making in one place so the viewer does not repeat the same setup for every part.
how: Helper functions create one shared material style, wrap shapes with shadow settings, and build simple shapes from primitives. Larger part builders combine those helpers. Substation parts are checked against a set, and other parts go to a shared model library.
inputs: Sizes (width, height, depth), positions and radii from each component's geometry data. The name of the part type. For substation parts, the list of substation part types.
outputs: Three.js groups and meshes that are added to the 3D scene.
risks: Zero or negative sizes are not rejected. Two beam end points at the same place produce a zero-length bar. The rest of the file was not read, so other risks are unknown.
debug: If a part looks wrong, check the size values passed in and then the matching builder in this file. If a part is missing, check whether its name is in the substation list or the model library.
